chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Barqī, from Jaʿfar, from Abī Ghassān Ḥumayd ibn Masʿūd, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about pelting the jamarāt while not in a state of taharah. He said: The jamarāt, with us, are like al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah—walls; if you were to go between them while not in a state of taharah, it would not harm you. But taharah is more beloved to me, so do not leave it while you are able to do it.
Thus, the correct understanding of this report is permissibility, and the first report is to be understood as referring to merit and recommendation.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, invoked here as a comparison in ritual ruling
key_terms.الْجِمَارُ: the jamarāt, the designated places pelted during hajj
key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَارِ: the ritual pelting of the jamarāt during hajj

ai.seo_question: Is taharah required for ramy al-jimar in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that taharah is not a condition for ramy al-jimar, and that performing it without taharah is permissible. At the same time, it emphasizes that taharah remains preferable and recommended when one is able.
